annotations.description: Lotus Bloom is a key card in a mill/combo deck running Tameshi, Reality Architect. Lotus Bloom can be suspended for free on turn 1, providing three mana of any color when it resolves — this is an incredible tempo advantage. It also synergizes directly with Tameshi's ability to return artifacts from the graveyard to the battlefield. Putting it on the bottom of the library as part of a mulligan/scry decision wastes a powerful synergy piece and free mana acceleration. The deck appears to be a mill/control deck where Lotus Bloom enables early Tasha's Hideous Laughter or Tameshi activations.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Lotus Bloom on the bottom of the library during the opening hand selection (appears to be a scry or partial paris mulligan putting cards back).
annotations.betterLine: Keep Lotus Bloom and put back a less impactful card like Stern Scolding or Into the Flood Maw. Lotus Bloom can be suspended turn 1 for free and provides massive mana acceleration, especially alongside Tameshi who can recur it from the graveyard.

annotations.description: Played the land (Cephalid Coliseum) before casting Hedron Crab, missing Hedron Crab's landfall trigger. This resulted in only 3 cards milled (from Ruin Crab) instead of 6 cards milled (from both Ruin Crab and Hedron Crab). In a mill deck, wasting 3 free mills is a meaningful loss of value.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Cephalid Coliseum first, triggering only Ruin Crab's landfall for 3 mills.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hedron Crab first using the existing Island, then play Cephalid Coliseum to trigger both Ruin Crab and Hedron Crab's landfall abilities for 6 total mills.

annotations.description: Exiled Whir of Invention (mana value 3) to Disrupting Shoal targeting Surgical Extraction (mana value 1). Since X=3 ≠ 1, the Disrupting Shoal will fail to counter Surgical Extraction. This wastes both Disrupting Shoal and Whir of Invention (the deck's key tutor) for nothing, while Surgical Extraction resolves and strips key cards from the graveyard/hand/library.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Whir of Invention (MV 3) to Disrupting Shoal, setting X=3, which cannot counter Surgical Extraction (MV 1).
annotations.betterLine: Exile Spell Snare or Into the Flood Maw (both MV 1) to set X=1 and actually counter Surgical Extraction. Spell Snare would be the better exile since Into the Flood Maw has utility as removal, and Whir of Invention is the most important card in hand.

annotations.description: Fetching Watery Grave and paying 2 life (going to 14) when an untapped Island was available as a choice. The mill deck primarily needs blue mana, and Grok4F Timmy already has Island and Cephalid Coliseum for blue sources. Paying 2 life is unnecessary when a basic Island would enter untapped for free and provide the same blue mana. The black mana from Watery Grave is only relevant for Drown in the Loch in hand, but Cephalid Coliseum already produces blue, and the opponent's graveyard has 10 cards making Drown castable with just UB. However, getting Watery Grave does provide the black source needed for Drown in the Loch. The issue is paying 2 life for it when Undercity Sewers (entering tapped) could provide both colors without life loss, or a basic Island could be fetched for free if black isn't immediately critical. Given that Drown in the Loch requires black mana and having it available is important for interaction, this is a close call, but paying 2 life when at 16 (already down from 20) in a mill deck that doesn't need to race is slightly suboptimal - Undercity Sewers entering tapped on their own turn when they likely don't need to cast Drown immediately would have been better.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Watery Grave untapped, paying 2 life (going from 16 to 14)
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Undercity Sewers (enters tapped but provides U/B with no life cost and a surveil trigger for graveyard value), or fetch a basic Island if black mana isn't immediately needed this turn
